Use case: stylized-concept.
Create ONE ORIGINAL transparent illuminated manuscript margin ornament for the Saltarello music score on the Polyhymnia homepage.
Reference image 1 is ONLY a structure reference: a slender vertical gold margin rod with a botanical branch going right at one end. Do not trace or reuse its old drawing.
Reference image 2 is the approved STYLE: use this exact rich hand-painted acanthus family, antique gold leaf and fine sepia outlines, lapis blue and vermilion red curled leaves, olive foliage, cream flowers with red centres, tiny berries and fine gold tendrils. Original art, not a collage.
Composition is a SQUARE transparent canvas. A slender straight vertical gold stem at exactly x=20% of canvas width, about 4% of canvas wide, with fine brick-red edging and a dark gold outline. Its quiet straight section must be gold with the same red edging along its length; no pink, no geometric bands. This is an elegant marginal stem, not a thick rectangular border. Richness comes from the floral terminal at one end. Most of the centre and right part of the canvas must stay empty for music. Any decoration beside the middle of the vertical stem stays in the left 28% of the canvas. Preserve true transparent alpha, no paper, no background, no shadow, no lettering, no musical symbols, no instruments, no frame around the canvas.
This is the UPPER terminal. The straight stem descends from (20%,20%) all the way to the BOTTOM edge (20%,100%), where it ends as a clean straight continuation with NO flower, cap or flourish. The TOP end becomes a graceful original blooming acanthus terminal: a cream rosette near (20%,14%), a cobalt and gold curling leaf above it, a vermilion leaf countercurl. A long tapered gold/olive branch grows RIGHT along the upper edge, reaching x=94%, with red and blue acanthus curls, two small flowers and delicate berry clusters. Keep this upper branching entirely in the top 32% of the canvas. One airy curl may dip to y=38%, confined to the left 45% of the canvas. Upper and left outer tips have about 3% transparent breathing room. A few modest small leaves can spiral around the left stem at mid-height, staying left of x=28%. End the rightmost horizontal tendril naturally; do not crop it. The top branch and straight stem must flow together as one organic drawing. Output only this one upper ornament.
